item.title: 'Best in world' Price set for Cardiff stadium fight
item.description:

Why it is here: original reporting, evidence and concrete detail

'Best in world' Price set for Cardiff stadium fight

She is already one of the most decorated fighters in British boxing history, and now Wales' Lauren Price is set to headline a summer stadium show at Cardiff City Stadium or Cardiff Arms Park.

Price dominated Michaela Kotaskova in Cardiff on Friday night, winning every minute of every round as she became Wales' first unified boxing champion by locking up the welterweight division.

With her stack of titles added to an Olympic gold medal, Price is now set to get to the next level, with negotiations already progressing for a stadium contest in the summer, with Chantelle Cameron or Mikaela Mayer â who fight on Christmas Eve â among the list of possible opponents.

The 32-year old Welsh fighter was so dominant in unifying the division on Friday it prompted her usually reserved trainer, Rob McCracken, to name her as the world's best female fighter, and now Price is set for a bumper 2027.

"If we can bring the big names and the big fights to a stadium, it's going to make a massive difference to Wales and Cardiff and everyone involved, and Lauren is very passionate about that," Price's promoter Ben Shalom told BBC Sport Wales.

"She is unique in the attention that she can generate and therefore I think she can demand to make sure that the fights happen in Wales.

"A lot of eyes will be on [Chantelle] Cameron and [Mikaela] Mayer's fight, and that is a fight [the winner versus Price] that we'd love to make.

"That fight in May or June at Cardiff Rugby Club or Cardiff City Football Club, you know, you're doing 15-20,000 ticket sales with Lauren Price there, so fingers crossed."

BBC boxing expert Steve Bunce says a deal for a stadium fight in the summer has been agreed, with a mandatory defence likely to come first in February. France's Emilie Sonvico has been touted as a possible opponent.

"She has a sneaky fight in February and then an outdoor fight in May or June, at Cardiff City Stadium, that's done and dusted, that's going to happen," he told BBC Sport.

"It won't be Claressa Shields in the opposite corner, but it will be a big opponent in May or June outdoors in the Welsh sunshine."

Price feels she needs to move to bigger capacity venues to secure her legacy, despite already being one of the most decorated fighters in British boxing history.

"It's about now moving on to what's next, and there is talks that it could potentially be a stadium fight in the summer, and that's what it's about now, the legacy and the fan base growing," she explained.

"My team know I will fight anyone."

'Best in the world'

Price's trainer McCracken, who runs the Team GB boxing programme, says the Ystrad Mynach southpaw is now the best female fighter on the planet and only likely to improve.

"Lauren's been an incredible female boxer for Great Britain; she's won the Olympics, she's won the World Championships, European Games, everything, every belt in boxing at welterweight," he told BBC Sport Wales.

"She is only going to do more and improve and gain from this experience; there's a massive journey still to come. She's only had 11 professional fights.

"She's done her bit, learned, developed and gained the experienceâ¦ and I feel she's the best female in the world.

"I have done for about 18 months, and I think she'll only improve and she'll only get better.

"In my lifetime, Joe Calzaghe is probably the best British professional I've ever seen, and I feel Lauren Price is the best female that I've ever seen. She's a super talent.

"There are bigger nights in Wales for Lauren and for everybody, and it will be a fantastic journey to be a part of."

item.title: Horse racing updates, news and results from Ascot, Haydock and more – live
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Matty’s Getaway has been rapidly reshod – props to the farrier – … and they are off and running in the 2.25 at Haydock …

Lossiemouth gives Mullins third winner at Punchestown, results from Ascot, Haydock and more – live

🏇 Live updates from all of Saturday’s major racing action

The top two in the market were both successful last time out. Matty’s Getaway took a 10-runner race at Chepstow on 11 October, coming nearly 10 lengths clear at the finish on soft ground, while Seaniecon led home a 19-runner field at Cheltenham’s October meeting.

It looks as though Matty’s Getaway has lost a shoe on the way to post. He’ll need to get that fixed before they can, er, get away.

There’s a bit more for the punters to get stuck into in the next race at Haydock, a handicap hurdle over three miles, with nine runners going to post following the scratching of Yellow Car.

Matty’s Getaway is the 100-30 market leader, with my fancy Seaniecon next in on 7-2 and Hartington on 4-1.

2.10 PUNCHESTOWN RESULT: LOSSIEMOUTH IN A CANTER

1. LOSSIEMOUTH (Paul Townend) 1-6 fav, 2. Blake. 4 ran.

Three to jump in the Morgiana Hurdle, Lossiemouth one-and-a-half up on William Munny, still the same order with two to jump …

Two out, Lossiemouth leads and starting to extend, she’s four up with William Munny being ridden …

Down to the last, Lossiemouth all on her own, going well clear in the closing stages … and it’s a flawless return for the champion!

Lossiemouth goes straight into the lead, William Munny tracks her in second …

Down past the stands and onto the second, Lossiemouth skips over …

Another slick jump at the third, and then the next ..

Off and running in the Morgiana Hurdle …

William Munny, the runner-up in the Supreme Novice Hurdle in 2025, is the only other runner in the four-strong field at a single-figure price. Barry Connell’s gelding is 7-1, and it’s 20-1 bar the two.

To no-one’s surprise, Lossiemouth can be backed at no better odds than around 1-7, if that’s your thing.

Most of us will, hopefully, just be watching on in admiration as one of the most popular horses in training returns for another campaign.

All eyes on the stunning setting of Punchestown in County Kildare now, as Lossiemouth, the champion over hurdles, makes her first start of the 2026-27 season in the Grade One Morgiana Hurdle.

She arrives with a career record of 15 wins from 19 starts including no fewer than 11 Grade One successes, and has finished second in three of her four defeats.

Freddie Gordon is talking to ITV Racing on the way back to unsaddle and suggests that Kocktail Bleu may now head over fences for a novice chasing campaign.

1.50 HAYDOCK RESULT: KOCKTAIL BLEU CHEER FOR BACKERS

1. KOCKTAIL BLEU (Freddie Gordon) 6-5 fav, 2. My Chiquita. 6 ran.

Down the back again, Kocktail Bleu takes over in front again, Miss Maverick makes a mistake six out …

Kocktail Bleu has built a useful lead over Smokeringinthedark …

Three to jump now, turning out of the back …

Into the straight, Kocktail Bleu leads over the third-last, My Chiquita has made rapid strides to join him …

The three of them are still together over the second-last, Kocktail Bleu back into the lead going to the last, he just needs to jump it …

And he does! Kocktail Bleu is going clear and it’s going to be a comfortable win.

Off and running in the 1.50 at Haydock …

Kocktail Bleu straight into the lead but it’s nothing like the fierce pace in the last race here ….

Miss Maverick is settled second, then there’s a gap back to Smokeringinthedark …

All runners travelling well and hurdling fluently …

Down the straight, Miss Maverick now goes on by a length from Kocktail Bleu …

Kocktail Bleu is going to go off at around 5-4 for this handicap at Haydock, Smokeringinthedark is the only other runner attracting any cash, at 9-4.

News arriving from Punchestown that the five-year-old Mighty Park was at the head of a 1-2-3 for Willie Mullins in the Beginners Chase.

He was ninth of 11 in last season’s Supreme Novice Hurdle but looks made for chasing and will head to a sterner target at one of the big Christmas meetings in Ireland according to his trainer.

He has a super jump in him. I’d imagine Mighty Park will stay at around two miles. I don’t think we’ll be going up in trip yet, we don’t need to.”

The well-fancied Manganese – priced up at around 11-2 – has come out of the handicap hurdle that is next up at Haydock, and Kocktail Bleu is a very warm favourite at around 6-4.

Smokeringinthedark is next in on 5-2, it’s 11-2 for Give It To Me Oj, and 10-1 bar the three.

1.30 ASCOT RESULT: KATEIRA FROM THE FRONT

1. KATEIRA (Tristan Durrell) 11-8, 2. Lucky Place. 3 ran.

Only two to jump, Kateira the narrow leader around the home turn, Lucky Place winding up to challenge …

Three in the air together over the second-last …

Down to the last, still Kateira in front, Lucky Place second, looks like that’s how they’ll finish …

A little surprisingly, Kateira leads with Lucky Place just behind, Fiveonefive brings up the rear …

Out onto the far side, no change in the order and all hurdling well until a slight error by Fiveonefive five out …

Kateira still leads four out, pace has been very, very steady throughout …

Off and running in the Grade Two Ascot Hurdle …

Kingofthefrontier was giving weight to his field in the last race, but it will be level-weights in the Grade One Formby Novice Hurdle at Aintree on Boxing Day if, as seems likely, that’s where he heads next. John Dawson is looking ahead in the winner’s enclosure:

We’re just feeling our way through. Our next plan would be the Formby. We just wanted to see if he was fast enough around here. He laid up nicely and as soon as Conor gave him a squeeze, he responded quickly.

The three-runner Ascot Hurdle is imminent at Ascot: the front-running Lucky Place is odds-on at around 4-7, and it’s easy to see Nicky Henderson’s gelding getting a very easy time of it on the lead.…

item.title: Washington Spirit vs. Kansas City Current: NWSL Championship preview
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: original reporting, evidence and concrete detail

The 2026 NWSL Championship is hours away from kickoff, with home side Washington Spirit vying for the NWSL Championship trophy for the third time in three seasons, this time with the Kansas City Current to beat.

Washington Spirit vs. Kansas City Current: NWSL Championship preview

Trinity Rodman and Temwa Chawinga headline the NWSL Championship match.

Both teams are star-studded with distinct styles that have brought them a lot of success this season. This matchup is guaranteed to deliver entertaining and high-quality soccer.

Kansas City is making their first finals appearance since 2022 hoping to win the trophy for the first time in club history. After winning the Shield last season with the best regular season record, the team made an unceremonious exit from the playoffs in the quarterfinals. This year, however, in the words of midfielders Croix Bethune and Lo’eau LaBonta, “It’s personal.”

Current head coach Chris Armas enjoyed his first season not only at the club, but in the league. His priority has been steadiness and continuity, trusting players to continue with the high-pressing and aggressively transitional style that has brought them a lot of success over the past three seasons.

In particular, forward Temwa Chawinga has scored two goals every three games this season when available thanks to her pace and technique up front. Her ability to speed past defenders, dribble through anyone in her way and shoot is so immense that even with three years worth of tape in the NWSL, teams struggle to contain her.

The Current also boast the newly crowned Midfielder of the Year, Croix Bethune, who broke a 10-year record for assists in a single regular season with 11. Bethune ranks high in the league in turnovers forced in the attacking and middle thirds of the pitch, making her the engine that kickstarts the transition chances that the team thrives on.

On the right wing, Michelle Cooper has similar pace and technicality to Chawinga on the left, making both sides of the pitch difficult for opponents to defend. Finally, striker Haley Hopkins, who scored the game-winner against Gotham FC in the semifinals, always finds herself in the right spot to clean up any leftovers created by her teammates or by botched clearances. Kansas City ended the regular season with the most goals scored in the league, and that wasn’t by accident.

On the defensive end, center backs Kayla Sharples and Gabby Robinson have led the team in limiting their opponents to only one goal so far in this post-season. Rookie right back Laney Rouse has been a revelation on both sides of the ball and stalwart left back Izzy Rodriguez contributes defensively while also delivering long balls with pinpoint accuracy in both live and dead ball situations.

Unfortunately for the Current, dead ball situations are the only ways they’ve managed to find the back of the net in the playoffs so far. A penalty in extra time won them the game against Angel City FC in the quarterfinals, and two free kicks were the difference between them and Gotham FC in the semifinals. Still, containing the offensive firepower that they do have can never be a guarantee for their opponents.

And perhaps fortunately for Kansas City, their opponents have only conceded set piece goals in their post-season so far.

Washington gave up two goals in their road to the finals, both of which came from corner kicks. The Spirit conceded the second-most set piece expected goals (xG) of all teams this season, beating only last place Chicago Stars. Players and staff alike from the Current have mentioned an emphasis on set pieces, and perhaps this strategy is the right one when they’re facing the second-stingiest defense in the league.

As for the Spirit, the team is benefitting from recently signed Clara Luvanga. The Tanzanian international striker made her debut for the team on Sept, 26 and has recorded seven goal contributions in seven appearances, including the game-winner in the semifinal against the Utah Royals. Luvanga has recently found chemistry with USWNT star Trinity Rodman.

On the defensive end of things, the Spirit have benefitted massively from the return of defensive midfielder Andi Sullivan from maternity leave, who has been key in cleaning things up in front of the defensive line and preventing opposing chances. The last time the Spirit played a final with Andi Sullivan as an active rostered player, they won their first ever championship back in 2021.

Also key are center backs Tara Rudd and Esme Morgan, with the latter leading all defenders in passing accuracy this season. Perhaps even more impressive is the fact that Morgan also leads defenders in passes into the final third. Her passing will play a huge role on Saturday against a high pressing team like Kansas City that is looking to force turnovers in dangerous areas. If Morgan can alleviate that pressure with line-breaking passes, the Spirit will both prevent the Current from attacking the way they like and find themselves in a favorable offensive position with their opponents caught too far forward.

Both teams vying for the trophy this weekend have very distinct styles of play that have brought them a lot of success, particularly at this crucial point in the season. The game will ultimately come down to which team succeeds at forcing the game to be played their way.

The Spirit do have home field advantage which is nothing to scoff at, especially at their ground which has been nicknamed “Rowdy Audi” for a reason.

So, while the Kansas City Current have put on an incredible end to their season, Washington end up having enough to win 2-1 in the final.

Source: SB Nation | Published: 2026-11-21 13:00 UTC | Difficulty: 60/100

'No big secret' – Pogačar also targets Paris-Roubaix in busy 2027

Surprising absolutely no one, Tadej Pogačar has said on record that he would like to return to Paris-Roubaix in 2027, where he hopes to finally crack the Cobbled Monument that has eluded him – but only just – in the past two seasons.

"It is no big secret that I would like to compete again," Pogačar told Sporza at a publicity padel event held by his agency. "I just want the entire season to be perfect again, and then we'll see."

News of Pogačar's 2027 goals have been a hot topic since he crashed out of the Vuelta a España having won three stages and led the race from the opening day. The five-time Tour de France winner has already said he will build his season around the French Grand Tour yet again, with the Haute-Savoie world title also high in his priorities, along with a return to the Vuelta. The UAE Tour has also been suggested as a season-opener prior to Strade Bianche, but a third Paris-Roubaix appearance has been kept quiet until now.

Victory at Paris-Roubaix would see Pogačar complete the Monument collection after his memorable, crash-affected Milan-San Remo success early in 2026. In his first and only two experiences of Roubaix, the Slovenian has finished second behind Mathieu van der Poel – despite crashing late in the race – and then Wout van Aert, the latter coming out of a two-up sprint in the velodrome.

Vollering is considering taking on all three Grand Tours in 2027

Earlier this week, retired pro Annemiek van Vleuten suggested that her young compatriot Demi Vollering might like to target all three 'Grand Tours' in 2027 as a way to one-up a 2026 season that has featured 18 wins in 33 race days, including four major Spring Classics, the Giro d'Italia, Tour de France Femmes, and finally, world and European titles.

"It will be very difficult for Demi to match this season," Van Vleuten told Wielerflits. "But perhaps she can try to win the three Grand Tours, because the Vuelta 's schedule is now positioned differently in the season."

Vollering has won the Vuelta twice before, but has never been able to combine all three major events. But in 2027, the Spanish stage race is moving from early May to September, immediately following the men's edition (which is itself starting a week later to make way for the Super Worlds in the Haute-Savoie), meaning that it can now more-comfortably be combined with the Giro (29th May - 6th June) and Tour Femmes (30th July - 7th August).

"It is certainly something I have discussed with the team," Vollering told NOS at a tribute event in her home town of Pijnacker, South Holland. "That move offers an option, so to speak. That if you win the Giro and the Tour, you can say: I can extend the season. If that is not the case, then you can skip the Vuelta.

"Personally, I am certainly really looking forward to racing again. Especially because it will be in that beautiful rainbow jersey; that gives extra motivation to train hard."

item.title: UCI sees no wrongdoing in Schreiber relegation, but Luxembourg federation considering further action
item.description:

Why it is here: original reporting, evidence and concrete detail

UCI sees no wrongdoing in Schreiber relegation, but Luxembourg federation considering further action

A little under two weeks after a devastating relegation saw Marie Schreiber lose the European Championship title to Lucinda Brand in Zeddam, Netherlands, the Luxembourg cycling federation (FSCL) has received a response from the UCI.

"They don't see that a bigger mistake has been made," the FSCL told Luxembourg's RTL. "The answer from the UCI was kept quite general and no further explanation was given."

There was widespread uproar following the elite women's race for which an official result took a long time to come through as the jury deliberated over Schreiber's deviation in the final two-rider sprint to the line. The resulting relegation was later questioned by Schreiber, her coach Sanne Cant, and several other big names throughout the sport, with Brand's own coach Sven Nys even expressing sympathy for the Luxembourg camp, which is not happy with the UCI's response.

"We do not want to simply accept this," the statement went on. "In our Board of Directors, we will now decide how we want to proceed. We do not want to close the file like this, and above all, we do not want to let the UCI close it so easily."

The FSCL may still take the case to CAS (the Court of Arbitration for Sport), but the wording of the final line above indicates also that they want a more detailed explanation of a rule that, in the 'cross regulations, invites varied interpretation.

15 mins. A clean lineout win from Itoje is moved quickly to Smith who finds another kick in behind for Joseph to chase. It’s a decent foot race but Bauden Barrett is first to it.

England v New Zealand: Nations Championship rugby union – live

🏉 Nations Championship updates, 2.10pm GMT kick-off

🏉 Follow us on TikTok | And email Lee about the game

Sat 21 Nov 2026 09.29 EST

First published on Sat 21 Nov 2026 08.15 EST

Sat 21 Nov 2026 09.29 EST

First published on Sat 21 Nov 2026 08.15 EST

13 mins. Sititi has a dart from the base of the scrum to set up an attack in the middle of the England half before Ref Berry blasts on his whistle as Heyes is suspected of a hip-drop tackle. The opportunity is wasted as Talyor overthrows the 5m lineout and Earl snaffles it. Van Poortvliet clears his lines.

10 mins. There’s no real benefit from the penalty lineout as the NZ defence are first to the breakdown to win a penalty of their own for England holding on. Roigard punts the ball upfield and a handling error in midfield hands a scrum to the All Blacks in enemy territory.

8 mins. The trademark of England’s attack recently has been the speed of recycling and then the absolute confidence to use the ball when presented to the backs. This is evident again on the latest possession before Furbank drills an exquisite 50:22 down the right touchline with barely 5 metres to play with.

An outstanding kick.

TRY! England 5 - 0 New Zealand (Henry Slade)

5 mins. Possession is retained by England from the penalty and some fast recycling hand Fin Smith an age to pick an angled grubber in-goal that Slade grounds.

Conversion is pulled left, but still a great start by the home side.

3 mins. England have their first attacking platform from a scrum just inside the NZ half. Joseph takes a solid carry into the line on first phase and this is enough to get the visiting defence moving backwards. The next few phases feature a rumble up by Earl before the ball is moved across the field and a desperate defence is already offside.

2 mins. Jordie Barrett is this close to grasping a long clearing kick from McKenzie after the All Blacks received the kick off. However, it bumps off his fingertips under a mid-air challenge from Will Joseph.

Officials for today, by the way

- Referee: Nic Berry (Australia)

- Assistant referees: Nika Amashukeli (Georgia), Damon Murphy (Australia)

- TMO: Marius van der Westhuizen (South Africa)

Kick Off!

Fin Smith sends the ball long from his boot and the game is underway.

HakaWatch!

Lewis Moody has joined the England team as they line up to face the haka. The home side move into a V formation to receive the challenge led by NZ captain Codie Taylor.

Moody sees off each England player in turn as he leaves the field with emotion clearly running high with each of them and he embraces them in turn. Quite the build up.

The teams assume the position for the anthems and sundry formalities. We’ll soon have the haka then a game of rugby will break out.

Out of the tunnel first is Beauden Barrett on the occasion of this 150th test, some achievement from some player.

Tommy Freeman out!

England are having to make a late change after the Northampton wing withdrew before kick-off

Apparently Freeman has been unable to shake off a thigh niggle, so Cadan Murley is in to make up the wide berths with Will Joseph.

Pre-match reading

Send all your thought to me, including your own best and worst compound nouns to me on the email up to and throughout the match.

Teams

England

George Furbank; Cadan Murley, Henry Slade, Seb Atkinson, Will Joseph; Fin Smith, Jack van Poortvliet; Fin Baxter, Jamie George, Joe Heyes; Maro Itoje (capt), Alex Coles; Ollie Chessum, Ben Curry, Ben Earl.

Replacements: Luke Cowan-Dickie, Ellis Genge, Will Stuart, George Martin, Greg Fisilau, Henry Pollock, Ben Spencer, Marcus Smith.

New Zealand

Beauden Barrett; Will Jordan, Anton Lienert-Brown, Jordie Barrett, Josh Moorby; Damian McKenzie, Cam Roigard; Ethan de Groot, Codie Taylor (capt), Fletcher Newell; Scott Barrett, Fabian Holland; Tupou Vaa’i, Peter Lakai, Wallace Sititi.

Replacements: Asafo Aumua, George Bower, Pasilio Tosi, Anton Segner, Leicester Fainga’anuku, Cortez Ratima, Richie Mo’unga, Rieko Ioane.

Preamble

Alastair Campbell has a book out called Persevilience, the title apparently a mash-up of perseverance and resilience (see what he did there) to form the worst compound noun since dorkburger. Although, one imagines the creator of the latter wasn’t trying to make it “the word the world needs now” like Big Al is on the cover of his volume.

However hateful the word, a still injury ravaged New Zealand need to show some of it today as they attempt to shrug off their seventy-three years in the making dorkburgering in Cardiff last week.

Since 1996, where the All Blacks have played tests with no more than a 21-day gap they suffered defeat in 52 first-up fixtures, with only 18 of the follow-up matches being a loss. Fourteen of those next-up losses were against either South Africa (10) or Australia (4), and they have only lost two consecutive matches on their November tours on one occasion in 2021 (Ireland, then France). On the 31 occasions they followed a defeat with a win, the week one loss margin average is seven points (sound familiar?) and the week two win margin is 26.

Thus, history tells us that such a situation tends lead to a rage filled bounceback being the order of the day, but matching the historic 26 point next-up winning spread will be a tougher ask than usual. The Dave Rennie led 2026 All Blacks are not the team of yore, and that’s before we consider their medical list, plus they must deliver it at SponsorDome Twickenham versus an England side on a decent run of form and results.

Exactly how good the home side’s run is can be debated;…
